title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section F, 'Application: differential interpretation of the special Teichmüller groups'.

Setting.
- X is a topological space with a finite discrete subset S (the word 'finie' is added above the line).
- X is a surface near S and carries a C^1 structure near S.
- G is a topological group acting continuously on the pair (X,S), by maps that are C^1 near S.

Tangent data, (124). For each x in S Grothendieck introduces two local tangent objects.
- S_{X,x} = S_x: in all likelihood the circle of tangent directions at x, (T_xX minus 0)/R_{>0}, i.e. the boundary circle of the real oriented blow-up at x.
- D*_{X,x} = D*_x: the punctured tangent plane (or punctured tangent disc) at x.
He sets S_S = ⨿_{x∈S} S_x and D*_S = ⨿_{x∈S} D*_x. G acts on these through differentials. Continuity of this derived action is not automatic for a topological group of homeomorphisms that are merely C^1 near S, so he adds it as a hypothesis. That is correct and necessary.

Universal covers, (125). For each x he chooses a universal cover D*~_x (a line-like object, homotopic to R covering the circle) and sets D*~_S = ⨿ D*~_x.

The group G~, (126). Forgetting the differentiable data for the moment, G~ is the group of pairs (u, ũ), where u ∈ G and ũ is a lift of the induced automorphism u_{D*_S} to an automorphism of D*~_S. The page ends with the projection G~ → G.

Next page. The kernel of G~ → G is T_S = ∏_{x∈S} T_x, where each T_x ≅ Z is the deck group π1(D*_x). This gives an exact sequence 1 → T_S → G~ → G → 1, which Grothendieck wants to make an exact sequence of topological groups. He then makes two reductions:
- He replaces G by the finite-index kernel of G → Sym(S), which permutes the points.
- G~ then becomes the fibre product over G of the single-point extensions 1 → T_x → G~_x → G → 1, so it suffices to treat card S = 1.

What it serves. This is the topological-group version of the central Z^n-extension that passes from the Teichmüller (mapping-class) group of a surface with n marked points to the group with tangential data, or boundary circles, at those points. The kernel is generated by the 'twists' around the punctures. Here the extension is realised concretely by lifting rotations of the tangent circles to their universal covers. Grothendieck calls these the 'special' Teichmüller groups in the Longue Marche, the groups attached to tangential base points.

The previous page belongs to the end of a preceding construction: the canonical identification (170) and its independence of auxiliary choices A, α.
errors: The transcription gives the projection as (u,ũ) ↦ ũ, G~ → G. The map to G must be (u,ũ) ↦ u, whether the slip is Grothendieck's or the transcriber's.
The page does not define S_{X,x} and D*_{X,x} (presumably they are defined earlier). The reading 'circle of tangent directions / punctured tangent plane' is inferred and not certain.

This page does not check that G~ is a group (lifts compose) or that the kernel is exactly ∏Z; this is done implicitly on the next page and is routine. Lifts exist because every homeomorphism of D*_x lifts to the universal cover.

ideas.what: Using C^1 data at the marked points (tangent circles / punctured tangent planes) to define tangential structure for a group acting on a surface with marked points
ideas.modern_name: Real oriented blow-up at punctures; tangential base points; framed / boundary mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tangential base points: Deligne (1989), Ihara; real blow-up: standard (A'Campo, Kawazumi, etc.)
ideas.where_published: The idea of the 'Teichmüller tower' with tangential base points is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984). The special Teichmüller groups appear in La Longue Marche (1981, circulated).

ideas.what: Extension of G by ∏_{x∈S} Z obtained from lifts of the induced action to universal covers of the punctured tangent planes
ideas.modern_name: Central extension 1 → Z^n → Mod(Σ_{g}^{n boundary}) → Mod(Σ_{g,n}) → 1 (capping sequence, kernel generated by boundary Dehn twists)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in mapping class group theory (Birman, Ivanov; see Farb–Margalit, Primer)
ideas.where_published: Possibly in La Longue Marche, in discrete form

ideas.what: Making the extension an extension of topological groups; reduction to G acting trivially on S via a finite-index subgroup, then to card S = 1 via fibre product of extensions
ideas.modern_name: Standard reduction for extensions (Baer-sum / fibre-product decomposition)

missed.claim: This is a definition of the 'special Teichmüller groups' for an arbitrary topological group acting on a surface with C^1 marked points, rather than for the discrete mapping class group. It realises the Z^n central extension through universal covers of the punctured tangent planes and seeks a topology on it. This continuous-group framework is a mild generalisation that does not seem to be written up in this form, but its content is standard.
missed.quote: Soit G un groupe topologique, opérant continûment sur (X,S), et respectant la structure différentiable au voisinage de S
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of minor interest as documentation of how Grothendieck tied tangential base points (in the Esquisse/Longue Marche sense) to differential data. The mathematics is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up a clean but standard construction: the Z^n-extension of a transformation group by twists at the punctures, built from universal covers of tangent data. Its value is historical (Grothendieck's own 'differential interpretation' of special Teichmüller groups) rather than new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The marked-point set is written with a script letter that the transcription renders as S; the next page writes I (T_I, card I). These are the same set.
In (126) the projection should read (u,ũ) ↦ u, G~ → G; 'quiest' should read 'qui est'.
In (125) the coproduct index should be x ∈ S, consistent with (124).
'on suppose' (marked [?]) fits the sense: the continuity of the action on S_S is a hypothesis.
In the first line of the text, 'finie' is an insertion written above the line.
